question: Can a filtered class-conditional GMM generator produce synthetic data that transfers better to real held-out data (smaller real-vs-synthetic gap) than a standard class-conditional Gaussian generator?
method: Train-on-synthetic, test-on-real logistic regression; baseline = class-conditional single Gaussian; improved = class-conditional 3-component GMM filtered by a real-vs-synthetic gradient-boosting discriminator. Seeds 42/43/44.

dataset.name: sklearn breast_cancer (Wisconsin diagnostic), stand-in for sperm-motion features

metric_name: test accuracy on real held-out data (train on synthetic)
baseline: Class-conditional single multivariate Gaussian generator fitted on training split; samples as many rows as real training data.
improved: Class-conditional 3-component Gaussian mixture generator; oversampled candidates are kept only if a gradient-boosting real-vs-synthetic discriminator (fitted on training data) scores them P(real) >= 0.5.
notes: Breast-cancer data is a stand-in, not the paper's sperm-motion data. Single stratified split; no hyper-parameter search was run (fixed defaults), so nothing was selected on test data. Filter fallback fills with top-scored rejects when too few candidates pass. Std is over 3 seeds only; differences may be within noise. Discriminator AUC uses fresh synthetic test-size samples.
